name: Wall push-up
form_cues: Place hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulders.
Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Bend elbows to bring your chest near the wall, then press away.
common_mistakes: Letting hips sag or stick out
Flaring elbows straight out to the sides
safety: Stand on a non-slip surface so your feet don't slide.
notes: Step feet further back to make it harder. Great first step for beginners and shoulder rehab.

name: Incline push-up
form_cues: Hands on a sturdy bench or counter, just wider than shoulders.
Squeeze glutes and brace so your body moves as one piece.
Lower your chest to the edge, then push the surface away.
safety: Make sure the chair or bench can't slide or tip before you start.
notes: The lower the surface, the harder it gets.

name: Knee push-up
form_cues: Kneel with hands under shoulders and hips in line with knees and head.
Lower until your chest is a fist's height from the floor.
Keep elbows about 45° from your body as you press up.
common_mistakes: Piking hips up into the air
Dropping the head toward the floor
safety: Use a folded mat under your knees if kneeling is uncomfortable.

name: Push-ups
form_cues: Hands just wider than shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, elbows at about 45°.
Push the floor away and finish with arms fully straight.
common_mistakes: Sagging hips or arching the lower back
safety: Stop if you feel sharp wrist or shoulder pain; try fists or handles to ease the wrists.
notes: Add a weight vest or plate on the back to progress; slow 3-second lowering builds strength.

name: Wide push-up
form_cues: Place hands about one and a half shoulder-widths apart.
Lower your chest between your hands, keeping the body rigid.
Press up while squeezing your chest together.
common_mistakes: Going too wide and straining the shoulders
safety: Keep the width moderate; very wide hands stress the shoulder joint.

name: Diamond push-ups
form_cues: Form a diamond with thumbs and index fingers under your chest.
Keep elbows close to your sides as you lower.
Press up until your arms lock out fully.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging as the triceps fatigue
safety: Move hands slightly further apart if your wrists or elbows complain.

name: Decline push-up
form_cues: Put your feet on a bench or chair, hands on the floor under shoulders.
Brace your core so your hips don't sag.
Lower your chest to the floor, then press back up.
common_mistakes: Head poking forward toward the floor
safety: Use a stable box or chair that can't slide out from under your feet.
notes: Higher feet shift more load to the shoulders.

name: Archer push-up
form_cues: Set hands very wide with fingers turned slightly out.
Shift down toward one hand while the other arm stays straight.
Press back up through the bent arm, then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips toward the floor
safety: Warm up wrists and shoulders well before loading one side.
notes: A key step toward the one-arm push-up.

name: Spiderman push-up
form_cues: Start in a strong push-up position.
As you lower, bring one knee toward the same-side elbow.
Return the leg as you press up; alternate sides.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips rotate or sag
Rushing so the chest doesn't reach the bottom
safety: Keep the movement slow if your hips are tight.

name: Hindu push-up
form_cues: Start in a downward-dog shape with hips high.
Swoop your chest low and forward between your hands.
Finish in an upward arch, then push hips back up to start.
common_mistakes: Collapsing into the lower back at the top
Bending the arms only, without the swoop
safety: Skip the arched finish if you have lower back pain.
notes: Traditional Indian wrestling exercise; pairs well with Hindu squats.

name: Dive bomber push-up
form_cues: Start with hips high and arms straight, like a downward dog.
Dive your chest close to the floor, sweeping forward.
Reverse the path back to the start instead of pushing straight up.
common_mistakes: Dropping straight down without the sweep
safety: Move slowly at first; it is tough on stiff shoulders.
notes: Unlike the Hindu push-up, the bomber returns along the same path.

name: Pseudo planche push-up
form_cues: Turn fingers out and place hands beside your waist.
Lean shoulders forward past your hands and keep that lean.
Lower and press while keeping arms locked in line at the top.
common_mistakes: Losing the forward lean as you push
safety: Warm up wrists thoroughly; the lean puts big stress on them.
notes: Main pushing drill for planche training.

name: One-arm push-up
form_cues: Spread feet wide and place one hand under your chest.
Put the free hand behind your back and brace hard.
Lower with control, keeping hips square, then press up.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to cheat the rep
safety: Build up slowly with incline versions to protect the shoulder.
notes: Elevate the hand on a bench to regress.

name: Typewriter push-up
form_cues: Set hands very wide and lower to the bottom of a push-up.
Slide your chest across to one hand, then the other, staying low.
Return to centre and press up.
safety: Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder at the bottom.

name: Sphinx push-up
form_cues: Start on forearms in a plank, hands slightly ahead of elbows.
Press through palms to straighten your arms.
Lower back onto the forearms slowly.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the hips instead of the arms
safety: Start from the knees if your elbows feel strained.

name: Tiger bend push-up
form_cues: Start in a handstand against a wall.
Lower onto your forearms with control.
Press back up to straight arms.
safety: Only attempt with a solid wall handstand and a soft surface.
notes: Classic old-school strength feat.

name: Scapular push-up
form_cues: Start in a high plank with straight arms.
Let your chest sink between shoulder blades, then push the floor away.
Keep elbows locked the whole time.
common_mistakes: Moving the hips instead of the shoulder blades
safety: Keep the range pain-free if you have shoulder impingement.
notes: Great warm-up for push-ups and handstands.

name: Pike push-up
form_cues: Walk feet in so hips are high and you form an upside-down V.
Lower the top of your head toward a spot ahead of your hands.
Press back up, keeping hips high.
common_mistakes: Letting hips drop into a push-up shape
safety: Lower slowly so you don't bump your head.

name: Elevated pike push-up
form_cues: Put feet on a box and walk hands back until hips are over shoulders.
Lower your head in front of your hands, forming a tripod.
Press up to straight arms, keeping hips stacked.
common_mistakes: Hips drifting back behind the hands
safety: Use a box that cannot slide; keep the neck neutral.

name: Planche push-up
form_cues: Hold a tuck or straddle planche with arms straight.
Bend elbows to lower your chest while staying parallel.
Press back up without losing the lean.
common_mistakes: Feet touching down during the rep
Shoulders not leaning past the hands
safety: Elite skill: build up over months and stop at any wrist or elbow pain.
notes: Parallettes ease the wrists; the tuck version is the usual first step.

name: Bench dips
form_cues: Hands on the edge of a bench by your hips, legs out in front.
Lower until elbows reach about 90°, staying close to the bench.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms.
common_mistakes: Dropping too deep and straining the shoulders
Letting the hips drift far from the bench
safety: Stop at 90° if you have shoulder issues; use a chair braced against a wall.
notes: Bend knees to make it easier, raise feet onto another chair to make it harder.

name: Bodyweight squat
form_cues: Feet about shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly.
Sit hips back and down, knees tracking over toes.
Stand by driving through the whole foot.
safety: Go only as deep as you can keep a neutral back and heels down.

name: Wall sit
form_cues: Slide down the wall until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Keep knees over ankles and back flat on the wall.
Breathe steadily and hold.
common_mistakes: Pushing on thighs with the hands
safety: Sit higher on the wall if your knees ache.

name: Sumo squat
form_cues: Take a wide stance with toes turned out about 45°.
Sit straight down, pushing knees out over toes.
Keep chest tall and squeeze glutes to stand.
safety: Only go as wide as your hips comfortably allow.
notes: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell between the legs to load it.

name: Hindu squat
form_cues: Swing arms back as you squat and let heels rise.
Touch fingers near your heels at the bottom.
Drive up, swinging arms forward, in a smooth rhythm.
safety: Stay on the balls of the feet only if your knees are pain-free.
notes: Traditional high-rep conditioning squat from Indian wrestling.

name: Cossack squat
form_cues: Start in a very wide stance.
Shift into one hip and squat deep while the other leg goes straight.
Keep the bent-side heel down and chest tall.
common_mistakes: Lifting the heel of the working leg
Rounding the back to get lower
safety: Hold onto a door frame for balance if needed.

name: Sissy squat
form_cues: Rise onto your toes and hold a support with one hand.
Push knees forward and lean back so hips stay straight.
Lower until knees are near the floor, then return.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips like a normal squat
Dropping too fast onto the knees
safety: Use a pad under the knees and skip it if you have kneecap pain.
notes: Strong quad isolation without any machine.

name: Box pistol squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg in front of a box, other leg reaching forward.
Sit back slowly until you lightly touch the box.
Stand up without rocking or using momentum.
safety: Lower the box height gradually as you get stronger.

name: Pistol squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg with the other straight out in front.
Reach arms forward and sink all the way down.
Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the free leg off the floor.
safety: Raise the heel on a small plate if ankle mobility limits depth.
notes: Holding a light weight in front can actually help balance.

name: Shrimp squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg and hold the other foot behind you.
Lower until the back knee touches the floor softly.
Drive up through the front foot, staying tall.
common_mistakes: Crashing the knee into the floor
safety: Put a cushion under the back knee while learning.

name: Skater squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg with the other bent behind you.
Hinge slightly and lower until the back knee touches a pad.
Push through the front heel to stand.
common_mistakes: Back foot touching down for help
safety: Reach arms forward for balance and keep the movement slow.
notes: Similar to the shrimp squat, but the back leg is free rather than held.

name: Split squat
form_cues: Take a long split stance, both feet facing forward.
Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor.
Push through the front foot to rise, feet staying planted.
common_mistakes: Stance too narrow, like walking a tightrope
safety: Hold a wall for balance if needed.

name: Bulgarian split squat
form_cues: Rest your back foot laces-down on a bench behind you.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is near parallel.
Drive through the front heel to stand tall.
common_mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench
safety: Use a stable bench that won't slide.
notes: Hold dumbbells to add load; listed here as the bodyweight version.

name: Forward lunge
form_cues: Step forward and lower both knees to about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and front knee over the foot.
Push hard off the front foot to return.
common_mistakes: Short step that pushes the knee far over the toes
Back knee slamming into the floor
safety: Use reverse lunges instead if forward steps bother your knees.

name: Reverse lunge
form_cues: Step back and lower the back knee toward the floor.
Keep most of your weight in the front heel.
Drive through the front foot to bring the leg back.
common_mistakes: Stepping back too narrow and losing balance
safety: Often the most knee-friendly lunge.

name: Walking lunge
form_cues: Step forward into a lunge, back knee just above the floor.
Push up and bring the back foot through into the next step.
Keep your torso tall and steps even.
safety: Clear a straight path free of trip hazards.

name: Lateral lunge
form_cues: Step wide to one side and sit hips back into that leg.
Keep the other leg straight and both feet flat.
Push off the bent leg to return to centre.
safety: Keep your toes pointing forward or slightly out.

name: Curtsy lunge
form_cues: Step one leg diagonally behind the other.
Lower until the front thigh is near parallel.
Push through the front heel to return.
safety: Shorten the step if you feel strain in the knee.

name: Bodyweight calf raise
form_cues: Stand tall, feet hip-width, fingertips on a wall.
Rise as high onto the balls of the feet as possible.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
safety: Hold a wall or rail for balance.
notes: Stand on a step edge for a bigger stretch.

name: Single-leg calf raise
form_cues: Stand on one foot on a step edge, heel hanging off.
Lower the heel below the step for a full stretch.
Rise as high as you can, pause, and repeat.
common_mistakes: Using the hand to pull yourself up
safety: Keep a hand on a rail or wall for balance only.

name: Tibialis raise
form_cues: Lean your back on a wall with feet a step out in front.
Pull your toes up toward your shins as high as you can.
Lower slowly without touching down fully.
common_mistakes: Feet too close to the wall
safety: Step feet further out to make it harder.
notes: Helps balance calf work and may ease shin splints.

name: Reverse Nordic
form_cues: Kneel tall with knees hip-width and toes flat.
Lean your straight body back by bending only at the knees.
Squeeze your quads to pull yourself upright.
common_mistakes: Going deeper than you can control
safety: Use a thick pad under the knees and start with a small range.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
equipment: Anchor for the heels (sofa, partner) and a mat
form_cues: Kneel with heels anchored under something solid.
Keep hips straight and lower your body forward as slowly as possible.
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to shorten the lever
safety: Start with a few slow negatives; expect heavy soreness the first week.
notes: Proven to reduce hamstring strain risk in sport. Can also be done with a GHD or a band for help.

name: Sliding leg curl
equipment: Towel or sliders on a smooth floor
form_cues: Lie on your back, heels on a towel, and lift hips into a bridge.
Slide heels out until legs are nearly straight.
Pull heels back under the knees, keeping hips high.
common_mistakes: Letting hips sink as the heels slide out
safety: Use on a smooth floor; stop if your hamstrings cramp.
notes: Also done on a stability ball.

name: Glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width.
Drive through the heels to lift hips until body is straight.
Squeeze glutes hard at the top, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
safety: Keep ribs down to avoid low-back strain.

name: Single-leg glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back with one foot planted and the other leg raised.
Push through the planted heel to lift your hips.
Keep the pelvis level, pause, and lower.
safety: Lower the range if you feel hamstring cramping.

name: Bodyweight hip thrust
form_cues: Rest your upper back on a bench, feet flat and knees bent.
Drive hips up until shins are vertical and body is flat.
Tuck chin and squeeze glutes at the top.
common_mistakes: Over-arching the back at the top
safety: Make sure the bench is against a wall so it can't slide.

name: Single-leg hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted, other knee pulled up.
Drive through the planted heel to lift hips level.
Lower with control without touching down.
common_mistakes: Pelvis dropping on the free side
safety: Keep the bench stable and the movement slow.

name: Frog pump
form_cues: Lie on your back with soles of the feet together, knees out.
Pull heels close and drive hips up.
Squeeze glutes hard at the top, then lower.
common_mistakes: Lifting from the lower back instead of the glutes
safety: Skip if the wide-knee position hurts your hips.
notes: Popular high-rep glute finisher.

name: Donkey kick
form_cues: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.
Keep the knee bent and push one heel toward the ceiling.
Stop when the thigh is level, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher
safety: Keep the movement in the hip, not the lower back.

name: Fire hydrant
form_cues: Start on hands and knees, back flat.
Lift one bent knee out to the side to hip height.
Lower with control, keeping weight even on both hands.
safety: Go only as high as you can without twisting the torso.

name: Clamshell
form_cues: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent, feet together.
Keep feet touching and lift the top knee.
Pause at the top and lower slowly.
safety: A common rehab move for knee and hip pain.
notes: Add a mini band above the knees to progress.

name: Table row
form_cues: Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge, hands shoulder-width.
Keep your body straight from heels to head.
Pull your chest to the table edge, then lower slowly.
safety: Test the table first: it must not tip or slide when you pull.
notes: Bend knees to make it easier.

name: Doorway row
form_cues: Grip both sides of a door frame, feet close to the threshold.
Lean back with straight arms and a straight body.
Pull your chest toward the frame by squeezing shoulder blades.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of staying straight
safety: Hold firmly; a slipping grip means a fall backward.
notes: Walk feet closer to the frame to make it harder. One-arm version works too.

name: Prone Y-T-W raise
form_cues: Lie face down, forehead resting, arms out in a Y shape.
Lift arms a few centimetres, thumbs up, then lower.
Repeat with arms in a T, then elbows bent in a W.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and arching the back
Shrugging instead of squeezing shoulder blades
safety: Keep the lift small and pain-free.
notes: Great for posture and shoulder health.

name: Wall walk
form_cues: Start in a push-up with feet at the wall.
Walk feet up the wall and hands back toward it.
Stop with chest near the wall, then walk back down slowly.
safety: Clear the area and keep a soft surface around you.

name: Wall handstand hold
form_cues: Walk up into a handstand facing the wall.
Push the floor away, ears covered by your arms.
Squeeze legs and glutes into a straight line.
safety: Practise on a soft floor; learn to roll or cartwheel out.
notes: Chest-to-wall teaches better alignment than back-to-wall.

name: Frog stand
form_cues: Squat down and place hands flat, shoulder-width.
Rest knees on the backs of your bent elbows.
Lean forward until feet float, eyes slightly ahead.
common_mistakes: Looking straight down and tipping over
safety: Put a pillow in front of your face while learning.
notes: Gateway to arm balances; yoga calls a similar pose crow.

name: Freestanding handstand
form_cues: Kick up softly with straight arms.
Balance using your fingertips and heels of the hands.
Squeeze legs together and keep a straight body line.
safety: Practise bailing out (cartwheel or roll) before kicking up away from a wall.

name: Handstand push-up
form_cues: Kick up into a handstand with your back to the wall.
Lower your head to the floor with elbows angled forward.
Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Crashing the head into the floor
safety: Place a folded mat under your head; build up with negatives first.

name: Freestanding handstand push-up
form_cues: Hold a steady freestanding handstand first.
Lower in control, keeping balance over your hands.
Press up while staying stacked.
safety: Elite skill: use a soft floor and know how to bail.

name: Press to handstand
form_cues: Start with hands down, hips high, legs straight or straddled.
Lean shoulders forward until your feet lift without jumping.
Raise legs slowly into a straight handstand.
safety: Requires good hamstring flexibility; warm up wrists and hips.

name: Planche lean
form_cues: From a push-up, turn fingers out and lean shoulders past your hands.
Keep arms locked and shoulder blades pushed apart.
Hold the lean without letting hips sag.
safety: Warm wrists well and build lean distance slowly.

name: Tuck planche
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, knees tucked tight to the chest.
Lean forward until feet lift, arms locked.
Round the upper back and push the floor away.
common_mistakes: Resting knees on the arms (that is a frog stand)
safety: Parallettes are kinder on the wrists.

name: Advanced tuck planche
form_cues: Start from a tuck planche.
Open the hips so the back is flat and level.
Keep arms locked and hips at shoulder height.
common_mistakes: Back rounding up like a regular tuck
safety: Build up over months; stop with any elbow pain.

name: Straddle planche
form_cues: Lean forward and lift legs straight and wide.
Keep the body parallel to the floor.
Lock arms and push the floor away.
safety: Elite skill; protect elbows and wrists with gradual volume.

name: Full planche
form_cues: Lean far forward with locked arms.
Hold legs together and straight behind you.
Keep the whole body level just above the floor.
safety: One of the hardest bodyweight skills; train years, not weeks.

name: L-sit
form_cues: Press hands down beside hips and lift your body.
Hold legs straight and level with the floor.
Keep shoulders pushed down away from the ears.
safety: Parallettes or dip bars make it easier than the floor.

name: V-sit
form_cues: From an L-sit, lean shoulders back.
Raise straight legs higher toward your face.
Push hard through the hands to keep hips high.
safety: Needs strong hamstring flexibility; progress slowly.

name: Elbow lever
form_cues: Tuck elbows into your belly near the hips.
Lean forward until the legs lift.
Hold the body straight and level.
safety: Put a cushion in front of your face while learning.

name: Dead hang
form_cues: Grip the bar shoulder-width and hang with straight arms.
Relax your shoulders while keeping a firm grip.
Breathe steadily and let your spine lengthen.
safety: Step down instead of dropping; skip if you have a shoulder dislocation history.
notes: Builds grip and decompresses the spine.

name: Scapular pull-up
form_cues: Hang with straight arms.
Pull shoulder blades down and back to lift yourself slightly.
Lower back to a full hang with control.
safety: Keep arms straight the whole time.
notes: Teaches the first part of every pull-up.

name: Flexed-arm hang
form_cues: Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar.
Hold, keeping shoulders down and chest up.
Lower slowly when you can't hold any longer.
safety: Use a sturdy box to get into position.

name: Negative pull-up
form_cues: Step up so your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself as slowly as possible, 3–5 seconds.
Reach a full hang, then step back up.
safety: Use a stable box to step up; expect soreness at first.

name: Band-assisted pull-up
form_cues: Loop a band on the bar and put a foot or knee in it.
Pull until your chin passes the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
common_mistakes: Bouncing off the band at the bottom
safety: Check the band for nicks and step out carefully.
notes: Use thinner bands as you get stronger.

name: Pull-ups
form_cues: Hang with an overhand grip just wider than shoulders.
Pull elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Lower to a full hang with control.
safety: Avoid if you have a shoulder injury flaring up.
notes: Add weight with a dip belt or vest once you can do 12+.

name: Chin-ups
form_cues: Grip the bar palms facing you, shoulder-width.
Pull your chest toward the bar, elbows down and in.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
safety: Ease off if your elbows or wrists get sore.
notes: Usually easier than pull-ups because the biceps help more.

name: Neutral-grip pull-up
form_cues: Grip the parallel handles, palms facing each other.
Pull your chest up between the handles.
Lower to a full hang.
common_mistakes: Neck craning to reach the bar
safety: Often the most shoulder-friendly grip.

name: Wide-grip pull-up
form_cues: Grip the bar about one and a half shoulder-widths apart.
Pull your chest up toward the bar, elbows out and down.
Lower to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Going so wide that range is tiny
safety: Don't go wider than is comfortable for your shoulders.

name: Commando pull-up
form_cues: Stand under the bar and grip it with hands close, one in front of the other.
Pull up, moving your head to one side of the bar.
Lower and alternate sides each rep.
common_mistakes: Hitting the head on the bar
safety: Move your head clear of the bar on every rep.

name: Towel pull-up
form_cues: Drape two strong towels over the bar.
Grip a towel in each hand and hang.
Pull up as high as you can, then lower slowly.
safety: Use thick, strong towels and check they won't slip off.
notes: Brutal grip builder for climbers and grapplers.

name: Chest-to-bar pull-up
form_cues: Start from a full hang.
Pull explosively until your chest touches the bar.
Lower with control.
safety: Build up from strict pull-ups first.
notes: Key strength step toward the muscle-up.

name: Kipping pull-up
form_cues: Swing between an arch and a hollow position under the bar.
Drive hips up at the end of the hollow and pull.
Push away from the bar to re-enter the swing.
common_mistakes: Kipping before you can do strict pull-ups
safety: Only kip once you have 5+ strict pull-ups; it is hard on the shoulders.
notes: Common in CrossFit for high-rep sets.

name: Archer pull-up
form_cues: Use a very wide grip.
Pull up toward one hand while the other arm stays nearly straight.
Lower and switch sides.
safety: Warm up elbows; the straight arm is under a lot of stress.

name: Typewriter pull-up
form_cues: Pull up with a wide grip until the chin clears the bar.
Slide across to one hand, then the other, staying high.
Return to centre and lower.
safety: Make sure your bar is solidly fixed; side-to-side force is high.

name: L-sit pull-up
form_cues: Hang and lift your legs straight out level with the floor.
Pull up while keeping the L shape.
Lower slowly without dropping the legs.
safety: Tuck the knees if the full L is too hard.

name: One-arm chin-up
form_cues: Grip the bar with one hand, other arm by your side.
Brace your body and pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
safety: Train elbows with lots of submaximal volume first; high tendon stress.
notes: Assist with a towel held lower by the free hand.

name: Tuck front lever
form_cues: Hang with straight arms and pull knees to your chest.
Press the bar down to lift hips to shoulder height.
Hold with your back horizontal.
safety: Warm up shoulders and elbows; stop if elbows hurt.

name: Advanced tuck front lever
form_cues: From a tuck lever, open your hips so thighs are vertical.
Keep the back flat and level.
Press the bar down with straight arms.
safety: Progress slowly to protect elbows and shoulders.

name: Straddle front lever
form_cues: Hang and lift your body level with legs straight and wide.
Keep hips in line with your shoulders.
Press down hard through straight arms.
safety: Elite skill; build up over months.

name: Front lever
form_cues: Hang and raise your straight body until horizontal, face up.
Keep legs together and glutes squeezed.
Pull the bar toward your hips with straight arms.
safety: Very demanding on elbows and shoulders; warm up well.

name: Skin the cat
form_cues: Hang and tuck your knees up through your arms.
Rotate backwards until feet point to the floor (German hang).
Return slowly the same way.
common_mistakes: Bent arms twisted on a bar
safety: Go only as deep as your shoulders allow; easier on rings than a bar.

name: German hang
form_cues: From a skin the cat, lower into the back position.
Let shoulders open gently with straight arms.
Keep breathing and come out slowly.
safety: Start with a few seconds; it heavily stretches the shoulder capsule.
notes: Prepares the shoulders for back lever.

name: Tuck back lever
form_cues: Enter through skin the cat with knees tucked.
Stop when your back is level, face down.
Keep arms straight and squeeze the chest down.
safety: Avoid if you have biceps tendon pain; straight-arm stress is high.

name: Back lever
form_cues: Enter from skin the cat and extend legs behind.
Hold your straight body horizontal, face down.
Squeeze glutes and keep arms locked.
safety: Build up through tuck and straddle versions to protect the biceps tendon.

name: Bar muscle-up
form_cues: Pull explosively, aiming the bar to your lower chest.
Lean over the bar and turn the wrists quickly.
Press out to a straight-arm support on top.
common_mistakes: Using a false grip on a bar (not needed)
safety: Needs a high, solid bar with clearance above it.

name: Human flag
form_cues: Grip a vertical pole with hands wide, top arm pulling, bottom arm pushing.
Lock both arms and lift your body sideways.
Hold your legs level with the floor.
safety: Use a fixed pole that cannot rotate; warm up shoulders well.
notes: No exact gear id for a vertical pole; pullupbar used as nearest.

name: Straight bar dip
form_cues: Support yourself on top of a straight bar with straight arms.
Lean forward and lower until the bar touches your upper belly.
Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Staying too upright and falling off
safety: Needs a solid bar at around hip height.
notes: Essential for the muscle-up transition.

name: Dip support hold
form_cues: Jump up to support on the bars with straight arms.
Push shoulders down away from your ears.
Keep the body still and legs together.
safety: Start with short holds if your wrists are new to it.

name: Chest dips
form_cues: Support on the bars and lean your torso forward.
Lower until shoulders are just below elbows.
Press up, squeezing the chest.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulders
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain.

name: Triceps dip
form_cues: Support on the bars with your body upright.
Lower with elbows pointing straight back.
Press up until arms are locked.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward (turns it into a chest dip)
safety: Stop at 90° elbow bend if your shoulders are sensitive.

name: Korean dip
form_cues: Stand with the bar behind you, gripping it overhand.
Jump to a support and lower as your hands go behind the body.
Push back up to the top.
safety: Needs good shoulder mobility; progress very gradually.

name: Parallette push-up
form_cues: Grip parallettes under your shoulders in a push-up.
Lower your chest below hand height for extra range.
Press back up to straight arms.
safety: Make sure the parallettes are on a non-slip surface.
notes: Neutral grip is easy on the wrists.

name: Banded push-up
form_cues: Loop a band across your upper back, ends under your hands.
Do a normal push-up against the band's pull.
Lock out hard at the top where tension is highest.
safety: Check the band for damage before each use.

name: Inverted row
form_cues: Hang under a bar at waist height, body straight.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing shoulder blades.
Lower to straight arms with control.
safety: Make sure the bar is locked into the rack safety pins or Smith hooks.
notes: Lower the bar or raise the feet to make it harder.

name: Archer row
form_cues: Grip wide under a low bar.
Row toward one hand while the other arm stays straight.
Lower and switch sides.
safety: Secure the bar before loading one side.

name: Ring push-ups
form_cues: Set rings a few centimetres off the floor and grip them.
Lower with rings close to your sides.
Press up and turn rings out slightly at the top.
safety: Start with rings higher to reduce the instability.

name: Ring support hold
form_cues: Jump up to support on the rings with straight arms.
Keep rings close to your hips.
Turn the rings out so palms face forward if you can.
safety: Use a box to get in and out.

name: Ring dip
form_cues: Start in a stable ring support.
Lower until shoulders are below elbows, rings close to the body.
Press back up and turn rings out at the top.
safety: Master ring support holds first; instability is high.

name: Ring fly
form_cues: Lean on the rings with arms nearly straight.
Open arms wide as you lower your chest.
Squeeze the rings back together.
common_mistakes: Bending the arms into a push-up
Going wider than you can control
safety: Start with rings higher and a steep body angle.

name: Ring triceps extension
form_cues: Lean forward holding the rings at forehead height.
Bend only the elbows to bring hands beside your head.
Straighten the arms to push back up.
safety: Steeper body angle = harder; start nearly upright.

name: Ring biceps curl
form_cues: Hold the rings palms up and lean back with straight arms.
Curl your hands toward your forehead, elbows fixed.
Lower slowly back to straight arms.
safety: Walk feet forward to make it harder.

name: Ring muscle-up
form_cues: Hang using a false grip.
Pull rings to the chest and lean the shoulders forward over them.
Transition into a dip and press to support.
common_mistakes: Pulling too far away from the rings
safety: Build strong ring dips and false-grip pull-ups first.

name: Iron cross
form_cues: Start from ring support and spread arms out to the sides.
Keep arms straight and press rings down.
Hold the T shape with body upright.
safety: Elite gymnastics skill; high tendon load, train with bands and spotting.
